chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Mahbub, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Every slave who is compared to [another] is free."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave who is compared to another in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing that a master's declaration comparing his slave to a free person (often interpreted as 'you are to me as my mother's back' or similar analogies) results in immediate emancipation. This hadith highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the literal efficacy of the master's intent and wording in manumission contracts, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of liberating slaves as an act of piety.
